title: GCP-961: feat(gcp): default ingress DNS + ingress-operator WIF service account
body:
## What this does

Adds automatic default-ingress support for GCP HostedClusters: the `*.apps` wildcard DNS is wired into the guest `dns.config`, an ingress-operator Workload Identity service account enables the guest cluster-ingress-operator to manage records via WIF, and the ACME DNS-01 challenge for the ingress wildcard certificate can be delegated to an external solver via an opt-in field.

Rebased onto current `main` (the generated artifacts and the GCP envtest suite were regenerated/merged; `make update` produces no drift).

## Commits (logically grouped for review / later split)

1. **feat(gcp): wire default ingress DNS zones into guest dns.config** — populates the guest `config.openshift.io/DNS` with the delegated `*.apps` base domain / zone names so the ingress-operator and router resolve correctly. Shared zone-name helper extracted to `support/gcputil`.
2. **feat(gcp): add optional ingress-operator workload identity service account** — new `spec.platform.gcp.workloadIdentity.serviceAccountsEmails.ingress` field (`+optional`, immutable, project-scoped CEL). HCCO provisions the guest `cloud-credentials` (external_account/WIF JSON) in `openshift-ingress-operator`, consumed by the guest ingress-operator (same Variant-B pattern as image-registry), skipped when empty. The ingress-op GSA gets `roles/dns.admin` only — no `compute.viewer`. The v2 e2e harness reads `ingress-sa` from `SHARED_DIR` and passes `--ingress-service-account`.
3. **feat(gcp): require ingress service account when Ingress capability enabled** — the CLI fails fast at create when the Ingress capability is enabled (the default) and no `--ingress-service-account` is passed; the hypershift-operator reports a non-blocking `IngressCredentialsFound` condition (reason `IngressServiceAccountNotFound`) for clusters created without the field via direct YAML. No hard error, so existing clusters and unrelated spec updates are unaffected. (A create-time CEL rule would need `optionalOldSelf` support in `FeatureGateAwareXValidation` — a controller-tools gap; the CLI check + condition cover the supported creation path.)
4. **feat(gcp): add opt-in ingress ACME challenge CNAME delegation** — new `spec.platform.gcp.delegation.acmeChallengeTarget` (`+optional`, GCP-gated: not present in the Default CRD; set-once: can be set at creation or added later, cannot be changed or removed; lowercase `_acme-challenge.` FQDN, ≤253 chars). When set, the CPO creates `_acme-challenge.<ingress domain>` → the target in the public ingress zone, so an external issuer (e.g. a central cert-manager with DNS-01 access to the target's zone) can solve the challenge for the `*.apps` wildcard certificate; the record name follows `globalconfig.IngressDomain(hcp)`, including the `spec.configuration.ingress` override. The `GCPACMECNAMEAvailable` condition (on the `GCPPrivateServiceConnect` CR and propagated to the `HostedCluster`) reports whether the record was published, or why it was not (`ACMECNAMEOutsideBaseDomain`, `ACMECNAMESelfReferential`). When unset, no record is created, and the record an earlier revision wrote unconditionally at the legacy name is removed — but only when its value matches, so operator-managed CNAMEs are preserved.

## Backward compatibility

- Both new API fields are `+optional` and platform-gated — CRD is backward compatible, N-1 safe (covered by a serialization round-trip test).
- No hard enforcement of the ingress SA: existing clusters and unrelated spec updates are unaffected.
- Existing clusters don't have `delegation.acmeChallengeTarget`: no record is created for them; the legacy `_acme-challenge.apps.<base domain>` CNAME written by earlier controller revisions is cleaned up (value-matched only). A deployment that relied on it can set the field at any time — adding it later is allowed, changing or removing it is not.
- The `GCPACMECNAMEAvailable` condition is absent unless the field is set, so it is not reported as `Unknown` on clusters that do not use the feature.

## Testing

- `make verify-ci` (generate/update zero-drift, staticcheck, fmt, vet, api-deps, crd-schema, docs-nav, tekton pairs, lint, git-clean) and `make api-lint` — clean; unit tests green.
- Envtest (full suite) on OCP 1.36.2 and 1.37.1 — green (355s / 347s). The GCP validation suite is extended with ingress-SA project-membership / immutability / capability gating, and ACME target format (lowercase, no trailing dot, per-label length), added-later, immutability and removal cases.
- Validated end-to-end on a dev GCP management cluster (ingress + console up, `*.apps` wildcard cert issued).
- `e2e-v2-gke` is green with both variants on 88e7fa9: https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results-public/pr-logs/pull/openshift_hypershift/9958/pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-v2-gke/2118060397993922560. The `gcp-ingress` specs pass (guest `dns.config` zone wiring, and a workload served through the default ingress controller).

## e2e (v2 framework)

GCP e2e runs on the v2 framework (`test/e2e/v2`). The GCP platform config now creates two static variants:

- `default` — unchanged: Console + Ingress disabled, runs `!lifecycle || gcp-worker-firewall`.
- `ingress` — **Ingress enabled** (Console disabled), runs the new `gcp-ingress` specs: it asserts the guest `dns.config` references the public and private ingress zones, and that a workload (deployment + service + route) is admitted under the ingress domain and served through the default ingress controller with HTTP 200. The request is made from inside the hosted cluster: the PSC endpoint fronts the management-side KAS load balancer, so the CI runner cannot reach the guest router.

`PreCreate` fails fast with an actionable message when `SHARED_DIR/ingress-sa` is missing. Two openshift/release changes are required, both merged: openshift/release#87114 runs the multi-cluster `create-guests` chain and has the `hypershift-gcp-hosted-cluster-setup` step write `ingress-sa` from the `create iam gcp` output (the `ingress-op` entry); openshift/release#88324 provisions one `PRIVATE_SERVICE_CONNECT` subnet per hosted cluster, because each cluster's PSC service attachment needs its own NAT subnet. The ingress paths are additionally covered by envtest, unit tests and the dev-cluster validation above.

+package gcputil
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"regexp"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// maxZoneNameLength is the maximum length of a GCP Cloud DNS managed zone name.
+const maxZoneNameLength = 63
+
+// zoneNameSuffixReserve leaves room for the longest suffix appended to the base
+// zone name ("-private" is 8 characters).
+const zoneNameSuffixReserve = 8
+
+// gcpZoneNameRegexp validates GCP Cloud DNS managed zone names: must start with a
+// lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.
+var gcpZoneNameRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`)
+
+// ValidateZoneName validates that a name meets GCP Cloud DNS managed zone naming constraints.
+func ValidateZoneName(name string) error {
+	if !gcpZoneNameRegexp.MatchString(name) {
+		return fmt.Errorf("zone name %q is invalid: must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens", name)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// truncateZoneName truncates a name to the specified maximum length.
+func truncateZoneName(name string, maxLen int) string {
+	if len(name) <= maxLen {
+		return name
+	}
+	return name[:maxLen]
+}
+
+// baseZoneName converts a base domain into the zone-name prefix shared by the
+// public and private ingress zones (dots replaced with hyphens, truncated to
+// leave room for a suffix).
+func baseZoneName(baseDomain string) string {
+	s := strings.ReplaceAll(baseDomain, ".", "-")
+	return truncateZoneName(s, maxZoneNameLength-zoneNameSuffixReserve)
+}
+
+// PublicIngressZoneName returns the GCP Cloud DNS managed-zone NAME of the public
+// ingress zone for the given base domain. The input MUST be the raw
+// HostedControlPlane base domain (hcp.Spec.DNS.BaseDomain), not a prefixed value,
+// so that it matches the name the GCP Private Service Connect controller uses when
+// it creates the zone.
+func PublicIngressZoneName(baseDomain string) (string, error) {
+	name := truncateZoneName(fmt.Sprintf("%s-public", baseZoneName(baseDomain)), maxZoneNameLength)
+	if err := ValidateZoneName(name); err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid public ingress zone name derived from baseDomain %q: %w", baseDomain, err)
+	}
+	return name, nil
+}
+
+// PrivateIngressZoneName returns the GCP Cloud DNS managed-zone NAME of the private
+// ingress zone for the given base domain. See PublicIngressZoneName for input requirements.
+func PrivateIngressZoneName(baseDomain string) (string, error) {
+	name := truncateZoneName(fmt.Sprintf("%s-private", baseZoneName(baseDomain)), maxZoneNameLength)
+	if err := ValidateZoneName(name); err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid private ingress zone name derived from baseDomain %q: %w", baseDomain, err)
+	}
+	return name, nil
+}
+
+// HypershiftLocalZoneName returns the GCP Cloud DNS managed-zone NAME of the
+// per-cluster hypershift.local private zone for the given cluster name.
+func HypershiftLocalZoneName(clusterName string) (string, error) {
+	name := truncateZoneName(fmt.Sprintf("%s-hypershift-local", clusterName), maxZoneNameLength)
+	if err := ValidateZoneName(name); err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid hypershift.local zone name derived from cluster %q: %w", clusterName, err)
+	}
+	return name, nil

+		{name: "When max is zero, it should return empty", input: "any-name", maxLen: 0, expected: ""},

+	for _, tt := range tests {

+// routeAdmittedHost returns the admitted host of the route, or "" when the
+// ingress controller has not admitted it yet.
+func routeAdmittedHost(route *routev1.Route) string {
+	for _, ingress := range route.Status.Ingress {
+		for _, condition := range ingress.Conditions {
+			if condition.Type == routev1.RouteAdmitted && condition.Status == corev1.ConditionTrue {
+				return ingress.Host
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return ""

+				Skip("Ingress capability is disabled on the HostedCluster")

+		})

+			tc := getTestCtx()
+			hc, err := tc.GetHostedCluster()
+			Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred(), "failed to get HostedCluster")
+			hcClient, err := tc.GetHostedClusterClient(hc)
+			Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred(), "failed to get hosted cluster client")

+			// The ingress operator creates the *.apps wildcard in the zones
+			// named here, so no record is published unless both are set.

+				g.Expect(dnsConfig.Spec.PrivateZone).NotTo(BeNil(), "guest dns.config should reference the private ingress zone")
+				g.Expect(dnsConfig.Spec.PrivateZone.ID).NotTo(BeEmpty(), "guest dns.config private ingress zone ID should be set")

+		})

+		It("should serve a workload through the default ingress controller", Label(internal.InformingLabel, "lifecycle"), func() {
+			tc := getTestCtx()
+			hc, err := tc.GetHostedCluster()
+			Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred(), "failed to get HostedCluster")
+			ingressDomain := ingressDomainForHostedCluster(hc)

+			restConfig, err := tc.GetHostedClusterRESTConfig(hc)
+			Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred(), "failed to get hosted cluster REST config")

+			Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred(), "failed to get hosted cluster client")

+			By("Waiting for the default IngressController to be available on " + ingressDomain)

+				ic := &operatorv1.IngressController{}
+				g.Expect(hcClient.Get(tc.Context, types.NamespacedName{

+					Name:      "default",
